title: Spec Templates Library
description: A curated library of reusable spec templates for common feature patterns. Instead of writing a spec brief from scratch every time, users pick a template (e.g. 'REST CRUD API', 'OAuth Login', 'Stripe Billing', 'Admin Dashboard') and get a pre-structured brief with sensible defaults they can customize. Templates are stored in the Direction Stack as L2 domain profiles so they're available across workspaces.

userStories.title: Template registry — define and store built-in templates
userStories.description:
Create a built-in template registry with 12 common feature patterns. Each template has a name, category, description, and a pre-filled brief string with placeholders. Templates are defined in frontend source (no backend needed — they ship with the app).

File: ~/rorca/src/lib/specTemplates.ts

Categories and templates:
- **Auth**: 'OAuth Login', 'Email/Password Auth + JWT', 'Role-Based Access Control'
- **Data**: 'REST CRUD API', 'GraphQL CRUD', 'File Upload + Storage'
- **Payments**: 'Stripe Subscription Billing', 'One-Time Payment Checkout'
- **UI**: 'Admin Dashboard with Data Table', 'Real-Time Dashboard (WebSocket)', 'Multi-Step Wizard Form'
- **Ops**: 'Background Job Queue'

Each template:
```typescript
export interface SpecTemplate {
  id: string;
  name: string;
  category: 'auth' | 'data' | 'payments' | 'ui' | 'ops';
  description: string;  // 1 sentence explaining what this builds
  brief: string;        // pre-filled brief with {{PLACEHOLDER}} vars
  defaultStoryCount: number;
  tags: string[];
}
```

Placeholders use `{{RESOURCE}}`, `{{APP_NAME}}`, `{{PROVIDER}}` format. Example for REST CRUD API:
```
Build a complete REST CRUD API for {{RESOURCE}} entities. Include list (paginated), get by ID,
create, update (PATCH), and soft delete endpoints. Add input validation with clear error messages,
workspace-scoped access control, and audit logging. Use existing DB patterns from the codebase.
```
acceptanceCriteria: src/lib/specTemplates.ts exports SPEC_TEMPLATES array with 12+ templates
Each template has id, name, category, description, brief, defaultStoryCount, tags
Brief strings use {{PLACEHOLDER}} format for customizable variables
Templates cover all 5 categories: auth, data, payments, ui, ops

userStories.title: Template browser UI — searchable grid with category filters
userStories.description:
Add a template picker to Spec Forge. When the user hasn't typed a brief yet, show a 'Browse Templates' button above the brief textarea. Clicking it opens a full-panel overlay (not a modal) with:

- Search bar: filters templates by name, description, or tags
- Category filter pills: [All] [Auth] [Data] [Payments] [UI] [Ops]
- Template cards in a 3-column grid:
  ```
  ┌───────────────────────────────┐
  │ 🔐 OAuth Login                │
  │ Auth                          │
  │ Add Google, GitHub, and       │
  │ Microsoft OAuth providers     │
  │                               │
  │ [Use Template]                │
  └───────────────────────────────┘
  ```
  - Icon (emoji per category), name, category badge, 1-line description
  - [Use Template] button — fills the brief textarea and closes overlay

- Clicking a template card (not just the button) previews the full brief in a right-side panel inside the overlay before committing

userStories.title: Placeholder variable substitution UI
userStories.description:
When a user selects a template that contains `{{PLACEHOLDER}}` variables, show an inline variable form between the template picker and the brief preview. The form auto-detects all unique placeholders in the brief and renders an input for each.

Example — REST CRUD API template has `{{RESOURCE}}` and `{{APP_NAME}}`:
```
┌─────────────────────────────────┐
│ Template variables              │
│ Resource name:  [invoices    ]  │
│ App name:       [MyApp       ]  │
│ [Apply →]                       │
└─────────────────────────────────┘
```

Once the user clicks Apply, all `{{PLACEHOLDER}}` instances are replaced in the brief string, and the filled brief is inserted into the Spec Forge textarea.

Implement in TemplateBrowser.tsx — detect placeholders with `/\{\{([A-Z_]+)\}\}/g`, deduplicate, render inputs, replace on Apply.

If a template has no placeholders, skip this step and fill brief immediately on 'Use Template' click.
acceptanceCriteria: Placeholder regex detects all {{VAR_NAME}} patterns in template brief
Unique placeholders rendered as labeled text inputs
Apply button replaces all occurrences in the brief string
Templates with no placeholders skip the variable form entirely
Brief textarea in Spec Forge shows the fully substituted text

userStories.title: Custom template creation — save any brief as a reusable template
userStories.description:
After a user writes a good spec brief, let them save it as a custom template for reuse.

In Spec Forge, add a 'Save as Template' button next to the brief textarea (visible when brief has 50+ characters). Clicking it opens a small inline form:
```
┌──────────────────────────────────┐
│ Save as Template                 │
│ Name:     [                   ]  │
│ Category: [Auth ▼]               │
│ Tags:     [                   ]  │
│           (comma separated)      │
│ [Save Template]  [Cancel]        │
└──────────────────────────────────┘
```

Custom templates are stored in localStorage as `rorcaCustomTemplates: SpecTemplate[]`. They appear in the template browser alongside built-ins, with a 'Custom' badge and a delete button (built-ins cannot be deleted).

Backend: no change needed — custom templates are local to the browser.

userStories.title: Template gate validation — all templates generate valid specs end-to-end
userStories.description:
Gate story for the Spec Templates feature. Validates that templates are wired up correctly end-to-end.

**Checklist (document in story notes):**
1. `npx tsc --noEmit` at ~/rorca/ root — 0 errors
2. Open http://localhost:5210 → Spec Forge → click 'Browse Templates'
3. Category filter 'Auth' → shows only auth templates
4. Search 'stripe' → shows Stripe Billing template
5. Click REST CRUD API template → right panel shows full brief with {{RESOURCE}} placeholder
6. Fill RESOURCE='invoices' → click Apply → brief textarea fills with substituted text
7. Submit → spec generates successfully
8. Save brief as custom template 'My Invoice CRUD' → appears in browser with Custom badge
9. Delete custom template → gone from browser
10. `npm run build` at ~/rorca/ root — clean build
11. `git add -A && git commit -m 'feat(templates): Spec Templates Library'`
